name: Stefano Ermon
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
research_topics: diffusion models and score-based generative modeling
reinforcement learning and preference optimization for generative models
diffusion large language models and discrete diffusion
generative foundation models for science (genomics, molecules, peptides)
Earth observation, remote sensing and geospatial representation learning
efficient generative architectures (video tokenizers, diffusion transformers, few-step samplers)
current_direction: Online RL and preference optimization to align diffusion models
Diffusion language models and test-time scaling for reasoning
Generative foundation models for biology (genomes, peptides)
Efficient generative architectures: tokenizers, grafting, few-step sampling
current_direction_basis: Inferred from the 2025-2026 items collected in this task, not from the older biography on the personal page. (1) RL/preference optimization for diffusion is driven by 'DiffusionNFT: Online Diffusion Reinforcement with Forward Process' (arXiv 2509.16117, Sep 2025), 'Divergence Minimization Preference Optimization for Diffusion Model Alignment' (arXiv 2507.07510, Jul 2025) and 'f-PO: Generalizing Preference Optimization with f-divergence Minimization' (AISTATS-25, listed on the personal page). (2) Diffusion LLMs / test-time scaling is driven by 'RFG: Test-Time Scaling for Diffusion Large Language Model Reasoning with Reward-Free Guidance' (arXiv 2509.25604, Sep 2025), 'Energy-Based Diffusion Language Models for Text Generation' (ICLR-25) and 'Reviving Any-Subset Autoregressive Models with Principled Parallel Sampling and Speculative Decoding' (arXiv 2504.20456). (3) Generative models for biology is driven by 'Genome modelling and design across all domains of life with Evo 2' (Nature, Mar 2026) and 'Zero-Shot Cyclic Peptide Design via Composable Geometric Constraints' (arXiv 2507.04225). (4) Efficient generative architectures is driven by 'InfoTok' (arXiv 2512.16975, Dec 2025), 'Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting' (NeurIPS-25) and 'Inductive Moment Matching' (arXiv 2503.07565). (5) Earth observation is driven by 'Earth Embeddings' (IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine, Jan 2026), 'TEOChat: A Large Vision-Language Assistant for Temporal Earth Observation Data' (ICLR-25) and 'Dynamic, high-resolution poverty measurement in data-scarce environments' (Journal of Development Economics, Nov 2025).

state_rationale:
DOWNGRADED from OPENING to OUTREACH on adversarial re-check (2026-08-31). WHAT HELD UP: the undergraduate-specific statement is real and I re-fetched it verbatim from the live page -- 'If you are a current or admitted Stanford undergraduate or M.S. student interested in research positions, please submit this form,' under its own '

Stanford Undergraduate or M.S. Students

' heading. It is present-tense and it is genuinely undergraduate-relevant, not a PhD-applicants-only line (the Ph.D. paragraph is separate and tells applicants not to make contact). WHY IT IS STILL NOT AN OPENING: the statement is purely a pointer, and the thing it points to cannot be verified. The forms.gle link resolves to a Google Form that returns HTTP 401 behind a sign-in wall; the form body never renders, so there is no evidence either that it is accepting responses or that it is closed. An unverifiable intake form is not a confirmed open position. Three further staleness facts argue against treating this as a live posting: the contact page footer reads 'Copyright (c) 2022'; the People page footer reads 'Copyright (c) 2024' and its entire 'Masters and Undergrad Students' section is commented out of the HTML (no undergraduate is displayed at all); and the public teaching list ends at Winter 2022/2023. This is a standing, undated invitation on an old page, not a currently-advertised opening with a deadline, project, term, or funding. WHY OUTREACH AND NOT WATCH: the lab is unambiguously active. Verified live in this task, the arXiv abstract page for 2509.16117 (DiffusionNFT) lists Stefano Ermon among the authors, submitted 19 Sep 2025 and last revised 16 Feb 2026; the personal publications page carries roughly a dozen NeurIPS-25 / ICLR-25 / AISTATS-25 entries. So a well-targeted approach is reasonable -- but it should be framed as outreach, not as 'apply now'. PRACTICAL NOTE FOR A STUDENT: eligibility is REQUIRED as worded (current or admitted Stanford undergraduate or M.S. student). Submitting the form is still the sanctioned channel, and a signed-in stanford.edu Google account will likely open it; a student should expect to confirm for themselves that it loads. No email is recorded because no literal address appears on any page fetched (see fetch_notes).
fetch_notes:
FETCH FAILURES / QUIRKS: (1) The supplied directory link https://cs.stanford.edu/people/stefano-ermon returned HTTP 404 ('The requested URL /people/stefano-ermon was not found on this server'), as did the trailing-slash variant. The www host works: https://www.cs.stanford.edu/people/stefano-ermon returned HTTP 200 and printed the exact title given in the task, so faculty_url uses the www form. (2) https://ermongroup.github.io/ returned a GitHub Pages 404; only the /blog/ subpath exists, and its newest post is 'Reflected Diffusion Models', 21 Apr 2023 — stale, so it contributed no evidence items. (3) The undergraduate Google Form https://forms.gle/EFNgNpZS3dQtR8qy5 returned HTTP 200 but the body is a ~35KB JavaScript deep-link shell (Google 'DurableDeepLinkUi'), not the form itself; no 'no longer accepting responses' string was present, but ABSENCE OF THAT STRING IS NOT PROOF THE FORM IS OPEN, because the form body never rendered. Open status is therefore unconfirmed. (4) profiles.stanford.edu/stefano-ermon returned HTTP 200 but the body above the fold was site chrome only; no additional facts were taken from it. (5) EMAIL IS OBFUSCATED at the source: the personal page contains the literal HTML 'Email: ermon AT cs.stanford.edu'. I recorded ermon@cs.stanford.edu by substituting '@' for the literal ' AT ' — a mechanical de-obfuscation of text that is literally on the page, not a guessed address. No mailto: link and no plain-text '@' address appears on any page fetched. (6) OpenAlex has TWO author records named Stefano Ermon (A5091179481, 456 works, Stanford; and A5113804858, 112 works). I used A5091179481 and independently re-verified authorship for every evidence item: the two arXiv preprints via their arXiv abstract pages, and the Nature / IEEE GRSM / NeurIPS-Grafting items via the OpenAlex authorships list. (7) The group site's own publications page stops at 2024, so all 2025-2026 publication evidence comes from OpenAlex and arXiv plus the 2025 section of Ermon's personal publications page. (8) Group site is dated: index/contact footers read 'Copyright 2022', people page reads 'Copyright 2024'. (9) The personal page's teaching list ends at Winter 2022/2023 and its 'Research Interests' block is HTML-commented-out; current_direction was therefore built only from 2025-2026 publications, not from that biography. (10) No grants, news items, or talks dated 2025-2026 were found on any fetched page, so no evidence items of those kinds are recorded. ===== ADVERSARIAL FACT-CHECK 2026-08-31 ===== (A) RECRUITING STATEMENT CONFIRMED GENUINE. Re-fetched https://cs.stanford.edu/~ermon/website/contact.html (HTTP 200). The raw HTML does contain '

Stanford Undergraduate or M.S. Students

' immediately followed by '

If you are a current or admitted Stanford undergraduate or M.S. student interested in research positions, please submit this form.

'. The previous agent's quote and its form-link attribution were both accurate. (B) THE FORM IS UNVERIFIABLE -- this is the reason for the downgrade. The prior note said forms.gle returned a 35KB JS shell; that is true for a browser UA, and worse, the shell Google served was a CACHED page for an UNRELATED short code (uyvxnM2LKR64YwEb7) -- our own code 'EFNgNpZS3dQtR8qy5' did not appear in the returned bytes at all, so no conclusion could ever have been drawn from it. Using UA 'curl/8.0' instead produces a real HTTP 302 to https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdawR-31I7-SlloymV0QYvzIR4eh1dUvTSGPA17LJtGvozzyQ/viewform?usp=send_form. Therefore open/closed status is genuinely unknown. For context, the sibling forms resolve and 401 identically: postdoc ZA39fKaYEmUiMyRw9 -> .../1FAIpQLScN0R3CnRkrmdO6OZ4LagefbipJD93sPd4puN48vwIxMVA5mw, visiting scholar RzTfiqFE8ocPwAGZ8 -> .../1FAIpQLScHqh5CkHSG_fijQljAqFHUDYWl8M63ds-fU8gJrc6MnM3I9Q.
